Let me analyze this OIML certificate markdown.

Document-level:
- Certificate number: R76/2006-A-NL1-20.55
- Scheme: A
- Project number: 2315156
- Page total: 2
- Member state: The Netherlands
- Date issued: 12 October 2020
- OIML issuer ID: NL1

Issuing authority:
- Name: NMi Certin B.V. (OIML Issuing Authority NL1)
- Address: Thijssesweg 11, 2629 JA Delft, The Netherlands
- Person responsible: M. Boudewijns
- Phone: +31 88 6362332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl
- OIML issuer ID: NL1

Applicants:
- Mettler Toledo GmbH, Im Langacher 44, 8606 Greifensee, Switzerland

Manufacturers:
- Same as applicant (labeled "Applicant and Manufacturer")
- Mettler Toledo GmbH, Im Langacher 44, 8606 Greifensee, Switzerland

Certified type:
- Category: Indicator
- Type designations: IND231, IND236, IND236-TLF
- Module designation: null (not mentioned)

Model family: cert covers 3 models: IND231, IND236, IND236-TLF. The characteristics table mostly has configuration axes (without tilt compensation vs with tilt compensation) rather than model differences. But note "12-36 V DC (only for IND236)" — power supply differs per model. Hmm. Should I emit model_family? The schema says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. The cert covers 3 type designations. But the characteristics vary mainly by configuration (tilt compensation), not model. The type designations themselves are models of the IND family. I think model_family with models IND231, IND236, IND236-TLF is reasonable. But then model_level entries would need values per model... The only model-specific attribute is power supply 12-36 V DC only for IND236. That's tricky. I could add a config_level for tilt compensation axis, and mention the power supply variants at type level as a list? Power supply voltage has multiple options: 100-240 V AC 50/60 Hz, 7.2 V DC battery, 9 V DC battery, 12-36 V DC (only IND236).

Per rules, 100-240 V AC 50/60 Hz → split into power_supply_voltage {min:100,max:240} V, power_supply_frequency {min:50,max:60} Hz, power_supply_type AC. Then alternatives: internal rechargeable 7.2 V DC battery, 9 V DC battery, 12-36 V DC (only for IND236). These are alternative power supply options — could be a components-like listing but probably best as separate type-level characteristics or a matrix_table. I think I'll emit:
- power_supply_voltage: value could be a list? The rules say lists of values should be a model matrix, but these are alternative configurations, not models. Hmm. I could use config_level with axis "power_supply_option" with conditions like "mains", "internal battery", "9 V battery", "IND236 external DC".

Actually maybe cleaner: type_level characteristics:
- power_supply_voltage_mains: {min: 100, max: 240}, unit V
- power_supply_frequency: {min: 50, max: 60}, Hz
- power_supply_type: "AC"
- load_cell_excitation_voltage: 5 V DC → value 5, unit "V DC" or split? "5 V DC" → value 5, unit_symbol "V DC" or "V"? DC is the type. I'll use unit_symbol "V" and maybe a note... Actually keep it simple: value 5, unit_symbol "V DC"? The rule example had "power_supply_type: {value: "AC"}" for AC. For load cell excitation, I'll just use unit_symbol "V DC" — hmm, better: value 5, unit_symbol "V". The DC part... I could add characteristic load_cell_excitation_type: "DC". That's a bit verbose but consistent.

- minimum_signal_input_voltage: config-dependent: without tilt compensation Umin = 0 mV; with tilt compensation Umin = 1 mV. That's config_level with axis "tilt_compensation".

- minimum_input_voltage_per_verification_scale_interval: 0.5 μV vs 3.33 μV → config_level, axis tilt_compensation.
- minimum_load_cell_resistance: 87 Ω vs 175 Ω → config_level.
- maximum_load_cell_resistance: 1200 Ω → type_level.
- fraction_of_maximum_permittable_error / apportionment? "Fraction of the maximum permissible error" = 0.5 → type_level: fraction_of_maximum_permittable_error, value 0.5, no unit.
- maximum_number_of_scale_intervals: config_level: without tilt comp n ≤ 6000 → {min: null, max: 6000}; with tilt comp ≤ 1500.
- maximum_number_of_weighing_ranges: 2 → type_level.
- weighing_ranges: "Single interval, Multiple range" — this is a list of supported configurations → could be type_level with value string "Single interval / Multiple range" or a config listing. I'll put as type_level: weighing_range_type: "Single interval or Multiple range". Hmm, it's a text value, fine.
- accuracy class: (III) or (IIII) → at recommendation level accuracy_classes: ["III", "IIII"]. Also maybe characteristics type_level accuracy_class. I'll put accuracy_classes in recommendation.
- temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C.
- load cell connection: 4-wire or 6-wire (remote sensing) without tilt comp; 6-wire (remote sensing) with tilt comp → config_level: load_cell_connection.
- cable length: "No special cable length / In case a 4-wire connection is used the load cells are connected directly without junction box" vs "17,3 m/mm²" → config_level: maximum_cable_length_per_cross_wire_section... value 17.3, unit "m/mm²" for tilt comp; text for without. Hmm, 17.3 m/mm² — that's cable length per cross-section. Unit symbol "m/mm²".
- application: with tilt comp "Intended to be used for on-board weighing", without "-". Could record as config_level application or type description. I'll include in config_level or skip. I'll include as config_level value with condition "without tilt compensation": value "-"? That's a non-value. I'll record only for with-tilt: condition "with tilt compensation", value "Intended to be used for on-board weighing". Actually maybe better as a string in config_level.
- software identification: Version number 1.xx.xxxx (x = 0…9) → type_level: software_version: "1.xx.xxxx".

Test reports:
- NMi-13200101-01 dated 22 April 2013, 49 pages
- NMi-13200101-01 dated 22 April 2013, 13 pages (duplicate number, different pages)
- NMi-14200515-01 dated 28 November 2014, 12 pages
- NMi-SO15202366-01 dated 26 February 2016, 8 pages
- NMi-2315156-01 dated 8 October 2020, 28 pages

role: type_evaluation_report (they are OIML Test Reports). The first could be type_evaluation_report; others test_report. All are listed as "OIML Test Reports". I'll mark first as type_evaluation_report and rest as test_report. Or all test_report. Given role options: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. I'll set the first as type_evaluation_report and the others as test_report.

Revision history: not present → omit.

Footnotes: none.

Date format: 12 October 2020 → "2020-10-12".

Config level entries: attribute, axis, values[] {condition, value, unit_symbol, footnote_markers}. The schema says config_level: attribute, axis, values: {condition, value}. Structured values rule applies — values must be objects with value/unit. So each entry: {"condition": "without tilt compensation", "value": {...}, "unit_symbol": ..., "unit_id": ...}.

Let me construct config_level:

1. maximum_number_of_scale_intervals, axis "tilt_compensation":
   - condition "without tilt compensation", value {min: null, max: 6000}, unit null (scale intervals are dimensionless counts; unit_symbol null)
   - condition "with tilt compensation", value {min: null, max: 1500}
2. minimum_signal_input_voltage, axis tilt_compensation:
   - without: 0 mV
   - with: 1 mV
3. minimum_input_voltage_per_verification_scale_interval, axis tilt_compensation:
   - without: 0.5 μV
   - with: 3.33 μV
4. minimum_load_cell_resistance:
   - without: 87 Ω
   - with: 175 Ω
5. load_cell_connection:
   - without: "4-wire or 6-wire (remote sensing)" — string value
   - with: "6-wire (remote sensing)"
6. maximum_cable_length_per_cross_section_between_indicator_and_junction_box_or_load_cells:
   - without: "No special cable length; 4-wire connection: load cells connected directly without junction box" — string
   - with: 17.3, unit "m/mm²"
7. application:
   - without: "-" (skip, not a value)
   - with: "Intended to be used for on-board weighing"

Should tilt compensation config also distinguish IND236-TLF? The TLF variant is likely the tilt-compensated one ("TLF" maybe truck load... for on-board weighing). But the cert doesn't state which model has tilt compensation explicitly. Don't fabricate. Keep axis generic.

Type level:
- accuracy_class: "(III) or (IIII)" — string. Also recommendation.accuracy_classes: ["III", "IIII"].
- maximum_number_of_weighing_ranges: 2
- weighing_range_types: "Single interval / Multiple range" — I'll name it weighing_range: value "Single interval or Multiple range"? Canonical label maybe "weighing_range_type". Value as string "Single interval / Multiple range".
- load_cell_excitation_voltage: 5, unit "V" — and maybe load_cell_excitation_type "DC". I'll do unit_symbol "V" and a separate note? To keep clean, I'll just do value 5, unit_symbol "V DC"? Rule says pull unit out; DC isn't a unit. I'll do unit_symbol "V" and separate characteristic load_cell_excitation: "DC"? Hmm — I think simplest: load_cell_excitation_voltage: {value: 5, unit_symbol: "V DC"}. But strictness... The example for power supply: "110-240V AC 50/60Hz" → split into voltage V, frequency Hz, type AC. Analogously: excitation voltage V, type DC. I'll add "load_cell_excitation_type": {value: "DC", unit_symbol: null, unit_id: null}.
- minimum... wait already config.
- maximum_load_cell_resistance: 1200 Ω
- fraction_of_maximum_permittable_error: 0.5
- temperature_range: {min:-10, max:40} °C
- power supply: multiple options. mains: power_supply_voltage_ac {min:100,max:240} V; power_supply_frequency {min:50,max:60} Hz; power_supply_type_ac "AC". Batteries: internal rechargeable 7.2 V DC; 9 V DC battery; 12-36 V DC (only IND236). I could make config_level axis "power_supply_option":
  - condition "mains AC": value {min:100, max:240}, unit V
  - condition "internal rechargeable battery": 7.2 V DC
  - condition "9 V battery": 9 V DC
  - condition "external DC (only IND236)": {min:12, max:36} V DC
  That's nice. axis: "power_supply_option". I'll do that for power_supply_voltage. And separate type_level power_supply_frequency for mains.
- software_version: "1.xx.xxxx" string, maybe with note. type_level: software_version: {value: "1.xx.xxxx", ...}.

Recommendation: id "R76", edition 2006, amendment null, scheme "A", accuracy_classes ["III", "IIII"].

Certificate: number "R76/2006-A-NL1-20.55", scheme "A", project_number "2315156", page_total 2, member_state "The Netherlands", date_issued "2020-10-12", oiml_issuer_id "NL1".

Matrix tables: none (table is characteristics, already captured). I could include matrix_tables for the characteristics table but it fits config_level. Skip.

model_family: include since >1 model. family_name: null. models: IND231, IND236, IND236-TLF. model_level: only model-specific attribute is 12-36 V DC only for IND236 — that's captured in config_level condition. I won't add model_level since no per-model attributes matrix. Actually maybe add a model_level note? Not necessary.

Components: none.

certified_type.description: "Characteristics of the indicator" — not really a description. Omit or set null. Omit.
